_info: Demo thresholds, not clinical. Each indicator cites its source in 'source'.
high: upper cuts for levels 1, 2 and 3. Level n if the value is greater than high[n-1].
low: lower cuts for levels 1, 2 and 3. Level n if the value is less than low[n-1].
inclusive: true turns 'greater than' into 'greater than or equal to' and 'less than' into 'less than or equal to'.
null: that level is not used for this indicator.
Team guide = 'AstroMed: Team Antares guide (NASA Space Apps 2026)'. 'Team criterion' = demo value with no external source.
nasa_ref: NASA requirement that sets the cut, or null if NASA does not publish a numeric limit for that indicator.
demo: cuts that replace the normal ones if the ASTROMED_DEMO environment variable is 1.
label and unit are in English: the engine writes its reasons in English (team decision, 2026-11-14).
rules_source: extra engine rules for that indicator (sustained readings, recovery after exercise, personal average) and where they come from.

heart_rate_bpm.label: Heart rate
heart_rate_bpm.source: Level 1 high: AHA, normal resting pulse 60-100 and tachycardia above 100 (https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/arrhythmia/about-arrhythmia/tachycardia--fast-heart-rate). Level 2 (120 and 45): team guide. Rest: team criterion.
heart_rate_bpm.rules_source: sustain_readings and sustain_seconds: level 2 or 3 needs at least 3 consecutive readings and 10 s between the first and the last. The firmware computes each pulse with a 10 s window and now sends every 2 s; counting only 3 overlapping observations would confirm too early. With the current board and the simulator, at least 6 readings at 2 s are needed; until then, a high reading gives amber, never green. Mixed high and low readings give amber with a notice to check the sensor. Reason: the photoresistor is noisy (electronics notes). exercise_recovery_s: for 5 min after a set of push-ups, or with activity 'moving', a high pulse at orange drops to amber; red (above 150) is not downgraded. All: team criterion.

body_temp_c.label: Body temperature
body_temp_c.source: Level 1 high: fever above 37.5 °C orally, Clinical Methods, NCBI (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK331/). Level 3 low: hypothermia below 35 °C, Mayo Clinic (https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/hypothermia/symptoms-causes/syc-20352682). Level 2 (38.0 and 35.5): team guide. Rest: team criterion.
body_temp_c.rules_source: sustain_readings: same as the pulse. A half-loose thermistor gives an isolated low reading, and that must not trigger red or an Earth summary. Team criterion. low_max_level: the thermistor sits on the wrist, and the skin cools with the surroundings: 'in warm conditions, skin temperature can be close to core body temperature, but several degrees lower in cold conditions' (Polar Research Center, 'Skin temperature', white paper, 16/06/2023, https://polar.com/img/static/whitepapers/pdf/polar-skin-temperature-white-paper.pdf). That is why a low temperature gives at most amber and asks for confirmation with a thermometer; a high one (fever) keeps its levels. Amber limit: team criterion.
body_temp_c.low_note: wrist reading; confirm with a thermometer

systolic_mmhg.label: Systolic blood pressure
systolic_mmhg.source: AHA/ACC: elevated 120-129, stage 2 hypertension from 140, severe above 180 (181 with inclusive is equivalent to 'above 180' in whole mmHg) (https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/high-blood-pressure/understanding-blood-pressure-readings). Level 2 is also in the team guide.
systolic_mmhg.rules_source: Level 2 needs two consecutive readings at level 2 or worse (team guide: 'escalate with 140/90 on two readings'). The previous one can be from any of the last 7 days; the latest must be from the last 24 h. 7-day window: team criterion.

diastolic_mmhg.label: Diastolic blood pressure
diastolic_mmhg.source: AHA/ACC: stage 1 from 80, stage 2 from 90, severe above 120 (121 with inclusive is equivalent to 'above 120') (https://www.heart.org/en/health-topics/high-blood-pressure/understanding-blood-pressure-readings). Level 2 is also in the team guide.
diastolic_mmhg.rules_source: Level 2 needs two consecutive readings at level 2 or worse (team guide: 'escalate with 140/90 on two readings'). The previous one can be from any of the last 7 days; the latest must be from the last 24 h. 7-day window: team criterion.

glucose_mg_dl.label: Glucose
glucose_mg_dl.source: ADA Standards of Care 2026: fasting, 100-125 prediabetes and 126 or more diabetes (https://diabetesjournals.org/care/article/49/Supplement_1/S27/163926/2-Diagnosis-and-Classification-of-Diabetes); hypoglycemia level 1 below 70 and level 2 below 54 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12690178/). High level 3 (250): team criterion.

mood.label: Mood
mood.source: Team criterion on the team guide scale (1 very bad to 5 very good). It is the only neuro indicator: there is no reaction test. Justification for the system: NASA HRP, isolation and confinement hazard (https://www.nasa.gov/hrp/hazards/).
mood.rules_source: personal_drop: amber if today's mood is 1.5 points or more below the crew member's own average over the previous 7 days, with at least 3 previous checks; it is added to the fixed cuts. Team criterion.

pushup_drop_pct.label: Push-up drop vs. own average
pushup_drop_pct.source: Level 2: NASA-STD-3001 vol. 1 rev. C, [V1 4024], muscle strength in mission is kept at 80 % or more of baseline; a drop of more than 20 % violates it (https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/nasa-std-3001-vol-1-rev-c-with-signature.pdf). Push-ups are used as an indirect measure of that strength. Levels 1 and 3: team criterion.
pushup_drop_pct.nasa_ref: NASA-STD-3001 vol. 1 rev. C, [V1 4024] Permissible Outcome Limit for Muscle Strength

still_for_s.label: Time without moving
still_for_s.source: Level 1 (600 s): team guide, threshold of the inactivity event. Level 2: team criterion.

cabin_temp_c.label: Cabin temperature
cabin_temp_c.source: Level 1 (25 and 20 °C): NASA-STD-3001 vol. 2, requirement [V2 6013] Crew Performance Environmental Zone, whose rationale gives 20-25 °C and 30-60 % humidity as the comfort and performance zone. Level 2 (27 and 18 °C): requirement [V2 6012] Crew Health Environmental Limits, 18 to 27 °C zone based on ASHRAE 55 (https://www.nasa.gov/reference/6-0-natural-and-induced-environments-vol-2/). Level 3 (32 and 15 °C): team criterion.
cabin_temp_c.nasa_ref: NASA-STD-3001 vol. 2, [V2 6013] Crew Performance Environmental Zone y [V2 6012] Crew Health Environmental Limits

humidity_pct.label: Cabin humidity
humidity_pct.source: Level 1 (60 and 30 %): NASA-STD-3001 vol. 2, requirement [V2 6013] Crew Performance Environmental Zone, 30-60 % humidity. Level 2 (75 and 25 %): requirement [V2 6012] Crew Health Environmental Limits, 25 to 75 % relative humidity zone (https://www.nasa.gov/reference/6-0-natural-and-induced-environments-vol-2/). No level 3.
humidity_pct.nasa_ref: NASA-STD-3001 vol. 2, [V2 6013] Crew Performance Environmental Zone y [V2 6012] Crew Health Environmental Limits

heat_index_c.label: Heat index
heat_index_c.source: NOAA/NWS: caution 80-90 °F, extreme caution 90-103 °F, danger 103-124 °F, converted to °C (https://www.weather.gov/ama/heatindex).

condensation_margin_c.label: Margin above dew point
condensation_margin_c.source: Team guide: medium condensation risk with a margin of 2 to 5 °C and high below 2 °C.

still_for_s.source: Team guide: the inactivity event uses 30 s in the demo and 600 s in real use. Level 2 (90 s): team criterion, same proportion as 600 and 1800 s.
